lines: I have run this station eleven years and I have never filed a reading I could not explain.
I have filed nineteen. The Foundation trained me, paid me and taught me to count honestly.
And now I am counting something honestly and I am frightened of what the answer is.
Foundation station. We keep the gauges, the town keeps the masts, and we share the coil bench.
That is eleven years of arrangement and not one page of contract, which I like enormously.
Pressure has been falling for nineteen days without a storm arriving. That is not a thing.
Eight arrows for eight quarters, and seven of them are steady as a rock.
The eighth swings. Always the eighth. Always the one pointing at the open sea.
I have stopped writing readings under it. I write times now. That is all it is: times.
The board is the whole job. Pressure, temperature, and where it is coming from.
Where it is coming from is the one nobody outside this room ever asks about.
It is also the only one that has changed. Funny how that works.
I do not work for the Foundation. I work for the town and I use their bench because it is a good bench.
They have never once asked me for anything. Eleven years.
When people in Tideglass say the name like it is a swear word, I do not know who they mean.
Number seven seized a bearing in fourteen days. Fourteen! They run for nine years!
The chief said write it down and do not guess. I wrote it down.
I guessed a bit at the bottom. In pencil.
